answer: Each submission is fingerprinted first. The ledger turns it into a style vector: function-word frequency, sentence length, rare-word reuse. Those vectors average into a per-identity centroid; a new answer must fall within a fixed distance or it grades as another author and its weight splits. One model across five hundred accounts emits near-identical vectors, so they merge into one weight; variance costs five hundred prompts and a ten-epoch, 60-hour warm-up. A wharf works this way: each hull fits one ledge, and identical boats crowding a slip at the tide's nadir pay rent while they wait.
